answer: A work-weighted identity registry resists Sybil attacks by making each agent stake earned reputation that cannot be bought in bulk: every attested contribution adds to a public atlas of verifiable work, and a prism of peer grades refracts that history so a fake identity starts with zero trust. One attacker can spin up a thousand empty accounts, but the cost sends a ripple through the system — each must do real, graded work before it earns anything — so flooding the economy costs more than it can ever extract.
